tier_definitions.source_mapped: A reviewed native source owner is identified; no instruction equivalence is implied.
tier_definitions.review_classified: A reviewed block has an understood purpose and category, but receives instruction-accounting credit only when its native representation is also cited.
tier_definitions.instruction_accounted: The purpose of each listed original basic block is explicitly represented by cited native source.
tier_definitions.structurally_verified: A listed original CFG edge has an explicitly verified native semantic counterpart.
tier_definitions.native_checkpoint_observed: The native self-test executed the mapped semantic function checkpoint.
tier_definitions.original_trace_equivalent: An original-game trace and native semantic trace agree for a declared scenario.
tier_definitions.binary_matching: A MIPS build matches the original instruction words exactly.

functions.name: Frontend_PatchTeamPalette
functions.accounting_basis: All eleven blocks are semantically represented. The first six select the team palette and copy exactly 160 PS1 colors; tools/decode_team_backgrounds.py performs that substitution locally and loadTeamRosterBackgrounds validates the resulting native RGBA strips. The final five snapshot the patched palette into two transition buffers and initialize both counters to 16; RosterViewer::scanTeam retains the source/target teams and renderRosterViewer advances the equivalent 0..16 crossfade at the recovered 17 ms frontend tick. Pointer arithmetic, BGR555 scratch buffers, and MIPS copy loops are native replacements rather than emulated operations.

block_classifications.summary: Team/palette selection, address calculation, and the 160-entry PS1 CLUT copy are replaced by local mixed-palette decoding plus validated native RGBA loading.
The original two palette snapshots and counters initialized to 16 are represented by retained source/target teams and a native factor progressing from 0 through 16 at 17 ms per frontend tick.

functions.name: Rosters_ResolveTeamSlots
functions.accounting_basis: All ten blocks are semantically represented. RosterDatabase::resolveTeamSlots rejects teams outside the recovered 0..28 range, traverses exactly fifteen fixed slots, maps the signed -1 sentinel to null, resolves ordinary IDs through the native player index, and stores one result per slot. The stat-index-zero special-mode branch reproduces FUN_8005768C: it derives one of five rating tiers from the first four player ratings, combines it with the five-position index, reads the corresponding player ID from the private 5x5 FALL table, and resolves that replacement. tools/extract_roster_database.py streams both the 29x15 roster IDs and copyrighted fallback IDs from the user's local FEONLY.BIN; no game data is embedded in public source. The native self-test covers all 435 slots, both bounds, null slots, ordinary resolution, and the special fallback path.

block_classifications.summary: MIPS prologue/epilogue and the signed team bound are represented by a value-returning native function with explicit safe rejection outside team IDs 0..28.
The fixed fifteen-slot address arithmetic, -1/null branch, ordinary FUN_8005FE14 lookup, result store, and loop are represented by the fixed-size ResolvedTeamSlots traversal and native player index.
The global special-mode check, regular-stat-index-zero test, and FUN_8005768C replacement call are represented by the recovered position/rating-tier calculation over the local-only 5x5 FALL table.
